description: Benchmark subsets of the agentic video detector WeVisForensics (wevis) and the same subsets scored by SynthScope's video detectors. Read by make_subsets.py, run_units.py, compare.py and the job scripts in this folder.
protocol: Held video benchmarks (GenVideo-Val, VideoPhy, VidProM, EvalCrafter): bench_eval_video --limit L with L = ceil(250 / n_generators), the first L sorted reals and the first L sorted fakes of every generator (video_layout.discover order); EvalCrafter has no reals and is paired with the first L GenVideo-Val MSR-VTT reals (the convention of the merged video matrix: --reals GenVideo/test/Crafter/0_real). GenBuster-Bench / GenBuster-Bench++ (the paper's GB / GB++): the first ceil(fraction * n) sorted clips of every folder (each generator's fakes and the one real pool), keeping the benchmark's real : fake composition. subsets/<bench>.json lists every file with its sha1. The agent and every comparator score byte-identical files.
internal_only_note: Comparators whose weights SynthScope does not redistribute (synthscope.hub.NEVER_REDISTRIBUTE). They are scored like the rest; compare.py also names the best publicly licensed comparator.

benchmarks.title: GenBuster-Bench (GB)

paper.source: WeVisForensics arXiv 2611.21373 Table 4 / Table 12 (GB, Acc. / R / F1)

benchmarks.subsample_note: Cost estimate (pilot job 295610, RTX A6000, ivi-cn023): 41.8 s per GenBuster clip (25 clips: 10 GB fakes over id / ood / wild, 5 GB reals, 5 + 5 GB++ clips). Full data = 3150 (GB) + 2000 (GB++) clips = about 60 GPU-h, over the 25 GPU-h allowance, so a documented subsample: the first ceil(0.4 n) sorted clips of every folder, 1260 (GB: 400 real + 860 fake) + 800 (GB++: 400 + 400) clips, about 24 GPU-h.

Full data = 3150 (GB) + 2000 (GB++) clips = about 60 GPU-h, over the 25 GPU-h allowance, so a documented subsample: the first ceil(0.4 n) sorted clips of every folder, 1260 (GB: 400 real + 860 fake) + 800 (GB++: 400 + 400) clips, about 24 GPU-h.

wevis.genbuster: IN-DISTRIBUTION for wevis: GenBuster-200K (the source of GenBuster-Bench) is in WeVisForensics' training data (arXiv 2611.21373 Sec. 3; GB is the paper's in-domain benchmark); GB / GB++ are not held out for wevis, the comparators were trained elsewhere.
wevis.genbuster_pp: IN-DISTRIBUTION for wevis: same BusterX family as GenBuster-200K, which is in WeVisForensics' training data (GB++ is the paper's out-of-domain set); not held out for wevis in the sense of the held subsets.

headline: The held-out headline is the mean over the four held subsets (genvideo, videophy, vidprom, evalcrafter). Means that include genbuster / genbuster_pp include in-domain data for wevis. On genbuster / genbuster_pp quote the pooled one-row-per-clip metrics (wild generators have 4-8 fakes each in the subsample).
